predecessors.name: Tughlaq dynasty
predecessors.text: Hasanabad (Gulbarga), taken from the Tughlaqs in the siege of 1346, and the Deccan the amirs held

successors.name: Bijapur Sultanate
successors.text: Yusuf Adil Shah's Bijapur, independent in 1490

successors.name: Ahmadnagar Sultanate
successors.text: Malik Ahmad Nizam Shah I's Ahmadnagar

successors.name: Bidar Sultanate
successors.text: the rump round Bidar under Qasim Barid I, who 'revolted' in 1492 and ruled the puppet Bahmani sultans (to 1527)

successors.name: Golconda Sultanate
successors.text: Telangana; the page says Golconda 'ended Bahmani rule after 180 years' in 1518

ledger.x: 1347: Raichur fort.
3 August 1347: Zafar Khan founds the Bahmani Sultanate.
1350: first campaign against Warangal.
1361: Golconda ceded.
1368: war with Vijayanagara over the doab.
By 1374 the Raichur doab goes to Vijayanagara: 'By 1374 Bukka Raya I...
1375: Cliopatria's 1375 shape adds the western strip to the 1358 box; no page opened dates it.
1407: treaty with Deva Raya I requiring annual tribute to the Bahmani Sultanate.
1417: 'The Sultanate invaded Vijayanagara in 1417 when the latter defaulted in paying the tribute'; the Bahmani page records a defeat in 1417.
1424: Ahmad Shah I at Warangal.
1425: the Warangal campaign ends ('Warangal (1424-1425)').
1427: Mahur annexed.
1429: the capital moves from Gulbarga to Bidar.
1429: the Konkan War.
1431: 'Finally, Ahmad Shah annexed Thana and Mahim from Bahmani Sultanate.'
1431: the Konkan War ends with Thana and Mahim in Gujarat's hands.
1435: Warangal and Rachakonda.
1435: Khandesh takes Berar.
1435: the Khandesh-Bahmani war over Berar begins with Nasir Khan's capture of Berar.
1437: Berar back.
1437: Nasir Khan is crushed at Laling and dies on 18 September 1437; the war over Berar ends.
1443: Alauddin Ahmad II defeats Deva Raya II (Chand Minar, 1445); the Vijayanagara page: 'wars broke out with the Bahmani Sultanate in 1443 with some successes and some reversals'.
1457: Gajapati attack.
1458: after a battle at Devarakonda 'the Telangana region became a feudal state of the Gajapati empire with the Velama chiefs as the vassal rulers'.
1461: Kapilendra's campaign to capture Berar (Achalpur) ends in retreat 'after Jaunpur's Husain Sharqi invaded Orissa'; the last Gajapati campaign on the page.
1469: Mahmud Gawan against Vijayanagara.
1469: the Konkan.
c. 1470: 'he temporarily allied his state with Vijayanagara around 1470.'
February 1472: Goa captured.
1490: Yusuf Adil Shah asserts Bijapur's independence ('agreed to assert their independence').
1490: Malik Ahmad Nizam Shah I asserts Ahmadnagar's independence.
1490: Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk asserts Berar's independence.

1491: the Bahmani state ends as a drawn power; in 1492 'Qasim Barid I revolted' and ruled the rump at Bidar, in 1518 Golconda 'ended Bahmani rule after 180 years' and the puppet kings were dissolved in 1527.

wars.name: Bahmani campaigns against Warangal
wars.outcome: 1350: Kapaya Nayaka cedes the Kaulas fortress; Mohammed Shah I 'successfully subjugated' Warangal and Vijayanagara (undated, gift of the Turquoise throne); Ahmad Shah I campaigned at Warangal 1424-1425.

wars.name: Bahmani-Vijayanagara wars
wars.outcome: Adoni 1368; Firuz Shah's victories 1398 and 1406; the 1407 tribute treaty; defeat in 1417; siege of the capital 1423; victory over Deva Raya II in 1443.

wars.name: Mahur campaigns
wars.outcome: Three campaigns in 1426 led to the annexation of Mahur by 1427.

wars.name: Konkan War (Gujarat and Bahmani)
wars.outcome: Gujarat annexed Thana and Mahim from the Bahmani Sultanate (Gujarat page).

wars.name: Khandesh capture of Berar
wars.outcome: Nasir Khan captured Berar in 1435; the Bahmani army crushed him at Laling and he died on 18 September 1437 (Khandesh page).

wars.name: Gajapati attacks on the Bahmani Sultanate
wars.outcome: Mahur and Bidar forts taken 1457, Devarakonda 1458 and Telangana made a Gajapati feudatory, Berar attempt in 1461 abandoned.

wars.name: Breakup of the Bahmani Sultanate
wars.outcome: Bijapur, Ahmadnagar and Berar asserted independence in 1490; Qasim Barid I revolted at Bidar in 1492; Golconda ended Bahmani rule in 1518.

certainty.note: No treaty line is recorded on the pages opened (the 1407 treaty set a tribute).
